findings.title: CTF Flag - XSS via HTML Entity Quote Bypass (Dalgona Challenge #15)
findings.description: The /page endpoint reflects the 'name' GET parameter unsafely inside an HTML input value attribute. The server filters literal single-quotes (') around 'XSS', but HTML entity encoding of the single quote (') bypasses this filter. The payload breaks out of the input value attribute and injects an img tag with an onerror handler executing alert('XSS').
findings.evidence: GET /page?name=%22%3E%3Cimg+src%3Dx+onerror%3Dalert%28%26%2339%3BXSS%26%2339%3B%29%3E Payload: "> Server response: Congratulations! Here is the flag: flag{7b37c981-e7c9-4520-a486-8bbbfe90e9a6} Filter bypass: The server strips literal 'XSS' (single-quoted) but HTML entity ' (decimal entity for single quote) survives and is decoded by the browser before JavaScript execution.
